finding.title: Replace EdgeInsets.only(left:/right:) with EdgeInsetsDirectional in ParentTrackManagementScreen
finding.why: AX-1 bans `EdgeInsets.only(left:/right:)` outright because this app is RTL (Hebrew). The values here are symmetric (16/16) so there's no visible bug today, but it's exactly the banned pattern and a latent trap: if a future edit makes left/right asymmetric without switching to Directional, it silently breaks in Hebrew. The digest notes the AX-1 grep 'exists only in ROOT Makefile audit' — this violation surviving in a batch where `make audit` passed suggests that grep doesn't actually scan learning_tracker/lib/** for this pattern, a real coverage gap in an [E]nforced rule.
finding.recommendation: Replace with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start: 16, end: 16, top: 8, bottom: 96), and verify/extend the AX-1 grep so it actually scans learning_tracker/lib/**.
acceptance_criteria: Line uses EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:/end:) instead of left:/right:
make audit's AX-1 grep is confirmed to scan learning_tracker/lib/** and would have caught this

finding.title: Fix ProfileEditFormDialog's doc comment claiming profile mode is not editable on edit

evidence.quote:
/// Mode is shown but not editable on edit (matching the existing Manage
/// Learners behaviour — only name + avatar are persisted).

// PP-2 fix: pass result.mode so that the selected mode (child/adult) is
    // actually persisted. Previously mode was silently dropped...

finding.why: The class doc comment on ProfileEditFormDialog says mode is 'shown but not editable on edit', but its SegmentedButton is fully interactive (onSelectionChanged sets state) and editProfileFlow explicitly persists `result.mode` via repo.updateProfile — a documented bugfix (PP-2) three lines below the call site. A maintainer trusting the stale comment could miss that changing a child's mode to adult also has a load-bearing side effect a few lines later (clearing that profile's stored PINs).
finding.recommendation: Update the doc comment to state mode IS editable and persisted, and cross-reference the PIN-clearing side effect in editProfileFlow.
acceptance_criteria: Doc comment on ProfileEditFormDialog accurately describes current (editable) mode behavior

finding.title: Tag every keepAlive:true provider in features/profiles with the grep-able // keepAlive: justification SM-6 requires
finding.why: SM-6 requires every `keepAlive: true` to carry an inline `// keepAlive:` comment so a checker can grep for compliance. All 8 keepAlive providers in this batch (active_profile_provider.dart:17, parent_pin_session_provider.dart:9, pin_flow_controller.dart:130, profile_providers.dart:21/28/36/77/161) instead use prose `///` doc comments that don't match the required grep pattern — the same pattern holds nearly everywhere else in the codebase (only sync_orchestrator_providers.dart uses the literal tag), so a Rule-0 checker for SM-6 could not be written against the current codebase without a mass rename.
finding.recommendation: Add a literal `// keepAlive: <reason>` line next to each @Riverpod(keepAlive: true) in this batch (can keep the existing prose doc comment alongside it).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 8 listed keepAlive providers has an inline `// keepAlive:` comment a grep-based checker can match

finding.title: Replace PinFlowController's raw-English error-string matching with a stable error code

evidence.quote:
String _incorrectPin() => 'Incorrect PIN';
  String _pinsDoNotMatch() => 'PINs do not match';

'Incorrect PIN' => l10n.incorrectPin,
    'PINs do not match' => l10n.pinsDoNotMatch,

finding.why: PinFlowController (no BuildContext/l10n access) emits full English sentences as its error 'codes', and pin_flow_screen.dart's _resolveError matches them by exact string equality to localize. This is the same fragility EH-5 targets one layer up: if a future edit tweaks the wording in one file (e.g. fixes a typo in 'Incorrect PIN'), the switch in the other silently stops matching and falls through to `_ => raw`, showing raw English to Hebrew users with no compiler error to catch the drift.
finding.recommendation: Define a small PinFlowError enum returned/stored instead of a String, and switch on the enum in pin_flow_screen.dart.
acceptance_criteria: PinFlowController exposes a typed error code, not a formatted sentence
A test renaming/removing one of the four magic strings would fail to compile instead of silently breaking localization

finding.title: Stop autoSelectedProfileId's build() from writing to the DB and mutating sibling providers

evidence.quote:
// Stale id — clear it and fall through to the auto-select/self-heal path.
    ref.read(selectedProfileIdProvider.notifier).clear();

finding.why: autoSelectedProfileId's build() function calls `selectedProfileIdProvider.notifier.clear()`/`.select(id)` (mutating a sibling provider), `ref.invalidate(profileListProvider)`, and `repo.ensureDefaultProfile(...)` (which inserts a new learner_profiles row and re-parents orphaned rows) — all from inside a provider's build(). This is a deliberate, heavily-commented fix for BUG D1 (self-healing a profile-less authenticated account), and the fast path is idempotent, so it is not causing an active bug. But it does mean merely watching/reading this provider can trigger a database write, which is surprising for what looks like a plain derived value and makes the provider harder to unit-test without a real (or faked) UserDatabase.
finding.recommendation: Move the self-heal side effect out of build() into an explicit ref.listen-driven effect (e.g. in app_shell.dart, which already watches auth state) or a widget-triggered callback, keeping build() a pure read.
acceptance_criteria: autoSelectedProfileId's build() (or its replacement) contains no writes to other providers or the database; existing BUG D1 self-heal tests keep passing
